headline: Fire erupts at drug factory in Tongi; 19 fire engines battle blaze
summary: A massive fire broke out at a pharmaceutical factory in Gazipur's Tongi on Tuesday morning. Emergency services are on the scene working to control the situation.
details: A fire broke out at a factory operated by Drug International Limited in Gazipur's Tongi around 10:15 am on Tuesday. Thick plumes of smoke were seen billowing from the site.
Nineteen fire service units were deployed to the scene and are actively working to extinguish the blaze. The army has also reportedly joined the efforts to control the fire.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage are yet to be determined. No casualties have been reported at this time.

headline_marked: [[Garment workers block roads]] in Uttara for third day, demanding Tk 30,000 minimum wage
headline: Garment workers block roads in Uttara for third day, demanding Tk 30,000 minimum wage
summary: Hundreds of garment workers have disrupted traffic in Dhaka's Uttara for three consecutive days, protesting for a higher minimum wage and increased allowances.
details: Garment workers have blocked roads in Dhaka's Uttara for a third consecutive day, demanding a minimum wage of Tk 30,000 and increases in other wages and allowances.
The protesters began their demonstrations on Monday, bringing traffic to a standstill in the Rajlokkhi area before moving towards the airport.
Traffic was significantly disrupted on Airport Road as workers continued their protest, according to police officials.
caption:
Dhaka's Uttara is experiencing major traffic disruptions for the third day as garment workers protest for a Tk 30,000 minimum wage.

Garment workers have blocked roads in Dhaka's Uttara for a third consecutive day, demanding a minimum wage of Tk 30,000 and increases in other wages and allowances.

The protesters began their demonstrations on Monday, bringing traffic to a standstill in the Rajlokkhi area before moving towards the airport.

Traffic was significantly disrupted on Airport Road as workers continued their protest, according to police officials.
